new_findings.title: Validated seal snapshot is not bound to authorization, QA, claim, and publication lineage
new_findings.evidence: The worker first parses and semantically validates seal A through _verify_seal(). _authorization_state() then independently reopens and hashes SEAL_PATH for the authorization seal hash and both QA lineage checks. It does not bind those checks to the exact seal bytes already validated. The worker later loads the numerical module using the stale in-memory seal A pin. Design verification similarly hashes DESIGN_PATH and then reopens it for JSON parsing.
adversarial_sequence: Present valid seal A and its static files while _verify_seal() validates and returns the parsed A object.
Replace the path with seal B and an authorization plus QA receipt pinned to B before _authorization_state(). B itself is not semantically revalidated in that call.
Restore the module bytes pinned by A before _load_sealed_numerical_module(seal_A).
Authorization and QA lineage now refer to B while the numerical module and historical-source contract are selected by A.
new_findings.impact: A concurrent replace/toggle can separate the independently approved seal identity from the seal that controls actual worker inputs and module loading. This is an authorization-lineage bypass even though the authorization file, QA report, and module each individually use held snapshots.
required_fix: Read the design and seal exactly once each into held byte snapshots; verify their expected digest and parse from those same bytes.
Return the validated seal digest together with the parsed seal from _verify_seal().
Pass that digest into _authorization_state and compare authorization.seal_sha256, QA pin seal_sha256, and parsed QA report seal_sha256 only to that value; do not reopen or hash SEAL_PATH there.

Thread the identical validated seal digest into preflight output, the permanent claim, worker launch/validation, result manifest, and terminal publication. Remove all post-verification _sha256(SEAL_PATH) calls.
Apply the same held-snapshot rule to design and execution JSON where a digest check is followed by a path reopen.
Add a synthetic adversarial test that swaps seal-path bytes between _verify_seal and authorization and proves fail-closed rejection before claim, materialization, or score.
Create a new prospective successor version and fresh truthful seal; do not mutate or authorize v2r3.
